cross_cutting_mbo_finding: ROUND-2 FINDING 1 - THE HANDOFF'S REAL PAYLOAD ON A PRINT DAY IS THE PRIOR FINAL-PHASE CONVICTION, NOT THE PRIOR CLOSE'S POSITION IN RANGE. I tested three candidate uses of the incoming exit state on my two days and only one survives. (i) SIZE THE OVERNIGHT LEG BY close_off_low: refuted. 0527 exits at 0.59 and its overnight ran -170; 0603 exits at 0.82 - more extended, so a give-back rule predicts a DEEPER fade - and its overnight ran only -70. Wrong ordering. (ii) CONTINUE THE PRIOR FINAL-HOUR CONVICTION THROUGH THE SEAM: also refuted. 0603's last hour is dir +1 / flow +1 = aligned BUY delivery, which predicts a positive overnight; realized -70. Both simple overnight rules fail on my own pair, so I do NOT re-size either overnight leg and I say so - the overnight is ~4 percent of session volume (ph1 vol 3305 and 3885 against 88726 and 82052 in ph2) and it is not where the handoff pays. (iii) THE FINAL-PHASE CONVICTION CONTRAST: this one holds and it is the whole gain. Across the four sessions in my two handoff pairs, an ABSORBED final phase delivers a POSITIVE terminal leg (0528 ph3 -3762 sflow under +160 px; 0603 ph3 -1442 under +350) and an ALIGNED final phase delivers a NEGATIVE-to-flat one (0527 ph3 -1575 under -370; 0604 ph3 -2816 under -90). That is 4 of 4, it is a direct instance of direction.flow_conviction_sign_gate applied to the last phase rather than the whole session, and it is the correct discriminator for the TERMINAL SHAPE - which is what the forward curve is scored on. My round-1 0528 path violated it: I carried C's 0527 crest-at-14:00-then-give-back shape onto 0528 even though 0528's final phase is absorbed and 0527's was aligned. The two must produce OPPOSITE terminal shapes. 0528's high printed AT the 18:00 bell (high_late true) with no give-back at all; 0604's high printed at 14:04 and faded 220 into the close. Corrected in r2.  ||  ROUND-2 FINDING 2 - I UNDER-APPLIED MY OWN CITED PLAY ON 0528. direction.absorption_is_reversal says in terms: 'Absorption is a REVERSAL against the absorbed side, NOT a damp in the nominal flow direction and never a cap: absorbed sell -> UP. Size to the reversal move.' In round 1 I read 0528's ph3 (3762 lots of sell absorbed under +160) correctly as a non-giveback and then sized it as 'a token positive, not an extension' at +80 - i.e. I treated absorption as a damp, which is exactly what the play forbids. Sized to the reversal move at the absorbed-phase scale the contrast set supports (~0.2x n0_net_sigma_5 = 150, cross-checked against the two measured absorbed final phases at +160 and +350) the leg is +150, not +80. That is the ONLY magnitude change I take on 0528: 1750 -> 1820. It closes 70 of the 350 and leaves 280 declined.  ||  ROUND-2 FINDING 3 - A LABEL CORRECTION I OWE ON 0604, AND IT SHARPENS THE CONTRAST RATHER THAN CHANGING THE NUMBER. My round-1 0604 text called ph3 'absorbed'. The evidence flag is ph_absorb [false, true, false] - ph3 is NOT absorbed; its conviction is ALIGNED NEGATIVE (-2816 sflow under -90 px). Correctly labelled, 0604's final phase is the session's ONLY genuine delivery and it is DOWN, in a session with no aligned-up phase anywhere. That is why 0604 crested at 14:04 and faded into the close while 0528 held its high to the bell, and it independently confirms my round-1 refusal of 0604's +1360 intraday high. The day-net is unchanged at 1050 (each of my four legs was within ~50 of realized; there is no leg with a mechanism error to fix), but the path is reshaped to express a 14:00 crest with a monotone fade rather than round 1's dip-and-recover.  ||  ROUND-2 FINDING 4 - THE SIGMA RULER IS A STALE VINTAGE AND THAT IS A SYSTEMATIC, ONE-DIRECTIONAL BIAS IN EVERY NUMBER I EMIT. B stood vol_regime down on my day as a 20260522 pre-ramp vintage the block exceeded at 3.16 sigma on 0528. I do not stand it down - it is the only ruler I have and without it the blind sized off nothing - but B is right about the direction of the error and it should be booked. The frozen block reads n0_net_sigma_5 737, n0_range_20_mean 1094, n0_range_20_max 2020, n0_prev_range 1400, with its own n0_activity_trend at 1.619 (the vintage DECLARES activity is expanding 1.6x). The block's realized ranges are 1190 (0603), 1650 (0604), 1720 (0527), 2840 (0528) - every one above the frozen 20-day mean and one at 2.6x it. So every leg I size as a multiple of 737 is biased LOW by construction. I explicitly DECLINE to rescale: n0_activity_trend is an ACTIVITY/volume trend and I have no measured mapping from it to a price-sigma multiplier, so multiplying 737 by 1.619 would be a fudge factor wearing a formula. The correct fix is a live-tape sigma at stage time, not a coefficient. Recorded as the honest, non-fitted explanation for why my residual is negative on BOTH days (-280 and -80) rather than random-signed, and handed to the merge as a DATA-PLANE item, not a play.  ||  ROUND-2 FINDING 5 - AN ANSWER TO B'S BLOCK-LEAN MECHANISM, TESTED ON MY OWN DAYS. B argues the lean is the blind's chain integrating its own error, so extension-gated plays read a suppressed cum and see room to fall. That is right for the BLIND and it does NOT explain my posterior's residual, and the merge must not conflate the two. My refine reads the REAL cum off the handoff: +450 into 0528 and +2070 into 0604. Run against structure.covering_extension_distribution_flip, +450 is the LOW-EXTENSION arm ('young/low-extension, cum low, age <=2: buyers absorbing a dip = short-covering UP'), which argued FOR my up on 0528 rather than suppressing it; and +2070 into 0604 fails the flip's conjunction anyway (it needs cum high AND age >=5 AND the absorption tell itself reversed - chain age was 0 and sell was still absorbed under a rising price). So extension gating suppressed NEITHER of my days. My residual is Finding 4 (stale ruler) plus the deliberately declined reactive tail, and nothing else.  ||  ROUND-2 FINDING 6 - THE EXTENSION-ROOM HYPOTHESIS FOR THE PRE-PRINT LEG IS REFUTED ON MY OWN PAIR, WHICH IS WHY I HOLD ONE RULE AT ONE SIZE. It is tempting to grade the pre-print de-risk leg by how much room the chain has: 0528 opens at cum +450 (low extension, room) and 0604 at +2070 (extended), so 0528's leg should be the larger. Measured low-to-print, 0528 ran +1120 and 0604 ran +1250 - the EXTENDED day's leg was the bigger one. Measured on the 06:00-10:30 clock they are +1060 and +1030, near-identical. One measurement contradicts the hypothesis and the other says the legs are the same size, so extension has no authority over this leg and I keep round 1's decision: ONE rule (1.36x n0_net_sigma_5, signed toward the crowded side's exit) at ONE size (+1000) on both days. Using one size on two days with wildly different COT crowding (1y-pctile 16.04 vs 0.94) and wildly different extension is what makes this a mechanism rather than two fits, and it is the finding I most want forward-tested.
